outcome: every command did what the runbook says, with the deviations forced by the machine and three places where the prose did not match what happened (corrected afterwards; no command changed). Step 0 printed its three sentinels and the session check (`6 names, 0 refused`; with DOCKER_HOST and PYTHONPATH in the session: two FOUND lines and `8 names, 2 refused`). The status command listed the pilot's processes with their words (TOOL, VF-EVAL, LAB, PROBE) and never a waiting shell. The stop command aimed at the waiting shell printed and signalled nothing; aimed at the tool it stopped the run in 6 s (traceback, KeyboardInterrupt, EXIT 130). After a hard kill of vf-eval the tool ended with `refused to go on: vf-eval died of signal 9 ...` and EXIT 98, the box was left, and the removal command refused a name nobody has and a container with another label before it removed the pilot's box. The disk watchdog refused at the runbook's own floor (EXIT 97, nothing started) and stopped a running rollout one second after the free space fell under the floor (one SIGTERM, containers removed by vf-eval, EXIT 97, a stopped record, nothing deleted). The clean pass of 2a, 2b and 2c gave the expected results, and step 4 copied five files and removed the two folders. The made-up credential file was not opened once in the whole rehearsal.
